e: Unknown. Compare duck (“to lower the head or body”) or jink (“to make an evasive turn”). Attested since the 16th century.
From Cantonese 粥 (zuk1) and Korean 죽 (juk). Doublet of zhou and juk.
From Gullah juke, jook, joog (“wicked, disorderly”).
